Do you like to cook? What's your favorite food to cook for yourself?

Steak! It's fast and delicious. I use some Montreal seasoning with extra peppers that I mix myself, and fry it in cast iron. I grill during the summer.

Or I knife-puree some garlic, add some salt and pepper, and cook it that way. I like ribeye steaks the most.
Rare, or blue-rare if it's a really good cut.

Gnocchi

They can be quite time consuming to make, even though it's simple (boil potatoes, put potatoes through ricer, mix with flour, roll out, cut, and cook), but the end result is always absolutely worth it.
With brown butter and fresh sage sauce perhaps? When I make gnocchi I make a big batch and freeze a couple of cookie sheets worth. four meals worth or so.

Steak's probably one of my favorite cause it's so quick and one of the best tasting. I coat the steak with olive oil then cover with salt and pepper. Put some olive oil in the cast iron and wait for it to start smoking then sear it for maybe 90 seconds each side till you get it all nice and caramelized. Top it with a chunk of butter and some seasoning and there you have it. I like it super rare too, crisp golden brown on the outside with best next to raw inside. So good.

I cook all kinds of fish very similar as well, just at a lower heat with lots of butter and some lemon pepper seasoning.. crispy flaky outside and juicy inside, it's so good I rarely even use tartar sauce or anything with it cause all the oil and butter with all the seasoning taste so good just on it's own.

Honorable mentions; spaghetti- my recipe takes a good 2 hours or more but I make a big pot and eat that shit for breakfast lunch and dinner throughout the week. Also sweet and spicy chicken breasts- cut into inch thick steaks and coat with a homemade brown sugar/paprika/cumin/oregano/salt&pepper seasoning, sometimes I'll wrap them in bacon too which is just something else.

I really enjoy cooking, it's a very useful skill to have and tons cheaper than buying stuff pre-packaged or going out to restaurants.

Fish of any kind. If it's skin on get your pan rippin' hot, add a small amount of oil, drop the fish in skin side down. Turn the heat off, and depending on the thickness of the fillet turn it over in 2-4 minutes, for just one minute longer.
Italian sausages in pasta sauce. Mozzarella cheese and one of those on a thick bun.

I fucking love to cook. For myself I usually prefer comfort food. Like a hamburger, spaghetti, a chicken breast with some baked potatoes and some greens. Soup is great too. Chicken veggie soup is probably what I make the most. Yeah, I can't pick one thing.

Chicken wings, deep fried, with Bufalo Sauce. Dry rub wings in: 1part smoked paprika 2parts chili powder 1/2 part each of cumin and coriander 3 parts celery salt. For a batch of 6 wings separated I use a teaspoon measure. For the buffalo sauce it is Frank's + sour cream to taste. Pint of beer and some yam fries. Yum.

This is my daily Sun-Fri meal schedule, Saturday is a cheat and food prep day.

Breakfast:

  • 4 oz of salmon fillet, season with black pepper, salt, various spices on hand, toss with panko bread crumbs and fry in a small skillet containing 1 Tbsp refined coconut oil

  • 4 oz frozen broccoli spears, season with black pepper and salt, toss in with the fish and brown, squeeze out the oil from the floret tops and save oil and dirty pan for lunch (the left over bits add flavor to the next dish)

  • 1 cup kefir

Lunch

  • 4 oz cut/chopped/sliced various veggies (broccoli, carrots, shittake, snap peas, watercress in a can, bell peppers, onion, etc.) season lightly and toss into frying pan used for cooking breakfast, cook to personal preference.

  • 2 oz of whole wheat pasta (weighed dry)

  • 2 oz of chicken breast (weighed pre-cooked) cooked with red onion (usually 2 small or one very large red onion per 6 portions) and cilantro (usually one bunch per 6 portions)

Dinner

  • 2 oz by volume (pre-cooked) steel cut oats cooked for 13 minutes, pinch of salt.

  • 1 egg (counted pre-hatched) cracked into oats after 13 mintues, mixed quickly, covered, and let sit for 10ish minutes (stove is off)

  • 1 apple

Usually I prepare all of this for an entire week, stuff the individual portions into ziploc bags, and freeze. Toss the individual portions into the fridge the night before and let them defrost. In the morning I cook breakfast and fry up the veggies for lunch. I used to buy frozen veggies; there is no pre-cooking required for them but they are mostly water and tasteless, fresh veggies require chopping, pre-cooking, cost more, but taste so much god damned better. Lunch stuff is thrown into a glass container and then nuked at work (chicken is cooked on saturday and frozen in portioned bags as well). For dinner more time is spent waiting than cooking. I workout in the morning and like the high protein meal upfront right after the gym, which leaves oatmeal for dinner...which aint too bad...all that fiber at the end of the day leads to a pretty healthy shit in the morning.

All in all, about 1,200-1,400 calories.

my fav thing to make myself is a bastardized Thai Curry. Panang Curry is my fav, red and yellow curry are allright, green is second fav but spiciest.

  1. get a pound of frozen stir fry veggies.

  2. half pound to a pound of protein. Ive done chicken, beef, tofu, or a combo. Shrimp would be aite too.

  3. A tub of curry paste. I use Ma Ploy brand from the asian market, and throw 3-4 tablespoons in there depending how hot i want it.

  4. a can of coconut milk.

  5. Rice

steps:

cook rice.

take cream out of the coconut milk, and start stir frying that shit. when you scrape the wok and it doesnt immediately close back up, its ready. throw the curry paste in there, and stir it up. Little darlin, stir it up.

throw your protein in the wok, and stir fry until almost done.

take protein out if you want, but im lazy so fuck it.

throw veggies in there and stir fry until they are done enough for your liking.

Somehwere in this general time frame, throw the rest of the coconut milk in there. adjust amount depending on how much sauce you want, or how soupy you want the curry. i have noticed the veggies add water to the situation, so not sure what to do about that. maybe drain some out if you have removed the protein. Like i said, laziness. It still tastes fine.

stir fry long enough to get everything hot.

serve over rice. it will be spicy.
